name: Tilt-shift macro lens (toy miniature look)
what: A post pipeline that makes a three.js scene look like a macro photograph of a toy: MSAA HDR scene with depth, ground-truth ambient occlusion, a one-pass gather bokeh depth of field whose plane of focus is tilted into a thin sharp band through your subject (occlusion-aware, cat's-eye bokeh), restrained bloom and an AgX filmic grade with warm white balance, grain, vignette and lens fringing. Quality presets and automatic resolution and preset step-down keep it running on phones.
use_when: the game should look like a photographed miniature, toy, tabletop model or diorama, or needs a filmic depth of field and grade with phone-friendly quality presets

third_party.what: Single-pass gather bokeh technique (reimplemented, no code copied)
third_party.author: Dennis Gustafsson

third_party.what: GTAOPass, UnrealBloomPass, FullScreenQuad, RoomEnvironment (imported from the three package)
third_party.author: three.js authors

good_for: Toy, marble, tabletop, miniature-city, diorama and model-railway games; any third-person or orbit-camera 3D game that wants a photographic, filmic finish; menus and flyovers that should look like a product shot.
not_for: Pixel, flat or painted looks; fast first-person games where blur hides threats; orthographic cameras; WebGPU renderers.
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-tilt-shift-macro, then replace renderer.render with lens.render(dt) through a drawWith hook in my-game/src/render/renderer.js and call lens.focusOn(player.position, 'play') each frame (see HOW-TO-USE.md).
